title: Factorization of curve modifications detected on contracted components
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed], and let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for each $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $C,X,Y,W$ be reduced $S$-curves, meaning flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $S$-schemes of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] whose local rings have no nonzero nilpotents, and assume their generic fibres are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $f:X\to C$, $g:Y\to C$, $a:W\to X$, and $b:W\to Y$ be $\eta$-modifications, with $fa=gb$. Here an $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], an isomorphism on the generic fibre and on schematically dense opens; an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense if $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. Assume that $Y$ is $\eta$-normal: every finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] $\eta$-modification of $Y$ is an isomorphism. If for every $s\in S$ every irreducible component of $W_s$ contracted to a point by $b_s$ is also contracted to a point by $a_s$, then there is a unique $C$-morphism $h:Y\to X$ with $hb=a$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3, printed p. 27, common-model component form. The proof uses normality of the target only to turn a finite eta-modification into an isomorphism, so eta-normality suffices (Proposition 3.5.2). No stability hypothesis is used.

proof.text: The generic point is open in $S$. If $V$ is a field take $t=1$; otherwise choose a nonzero $t$ in the least nonzero prime of its finite prime chain. Every nonzero prime contains $t$, so $D(t)=\eta$ and $V[1/t]=K$. For $Z=W,Y$ and every affine open $A\subseteq Z$, apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] to the flat scheme $A$ and its invertible module $\mathcal O_A$. Every nonzero element of $V$ acts injectively on $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$; hence this ring injects into its localization at $t$. Thus $Z_\eta$ is schematically dense in $Z$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction: finite-height valuation generic open and flat generic schematic density, using the cited torsion-free-sections statement.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_CY$ and let $q:P\to X$, $p_0:P\to Y$ be the projections. Since $f_\eta,g_\eta$ are isomorphisms, $U=P_\eta\cong Y_\eta$ is exactly the common generic graph. Its inclusion is a quasi-compact open immersion: on each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset P$ it is $D(t)$. Form its scheme-theoretic closure $i:\Gamma\hookrightarrow P$ by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. Explicitly, on this affine chart its ideal is $I=\ker(A\to A[1/t])$. These ideals commute with localization, so give the closed subscheme; $I[1/t]=0$ and $(A/I)[1/t]=A[1/t]$. Moreover $A/I\to A[1/t]$ is injective. Thus $\Gamma_\eta=U$ and $U$ is schematically dense in $\Gamma$. Any ideal defining a closed subscheme containing $U$ has zero localization and is contained in $I$; this identifies the constructed subscheme with the smallest closure of [lemma-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure-minimal].

source.place: Agent affine calculation following example-scheme-theoretic-closure; quasi-compact immersion closure and its minimality.

proof.text: The compatible maps give $c=(a,b):W\to P$. A local section of the ideal of $\Gamma$ vanishes on $U$, so its pullback under $c$ vanishes on $W_\eta$. By the injectivity proved in step 1 it is zero on $W$. Thus the pulled-back defining ideal is zero and $c$ factors uniquely as $i\circ r$ for $r:W\to\Gamma$. Write $p=p_0i$ and $q_\Gamma=qi$. Then $pr=b$ and $q_\Gamma r=a$, and $r_\eta$ is an isomorphism onto $U$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction: scheme-theoretic factorization through the generic graph closure by the vanishing of its defining ideal.

proof.text: The projection $p_0:P\to Y$ is the base change of the proper map $f:X\to C$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). The closure inclusion $i$ is closed, hence proper by its clause (c), so $p=p_0i$ is proper by clause (a). In particular $p$ is separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Since $Y\to S$ is of finite presentation, it is of finite type; the composite $\Gamma\to S$ is locally of finite type by clause (e). It is also quasi-compact: over a quasi-compact open in $S$, cover its inverse image in $Y$ by finitely many affine opens and then use quasi-compactness of $p$ on each. Thus the composite is of finite type. Consequently each $\Gamma_s$ is of finite type over $\kappa(s)$: affine charts are obtained by tensoring finitely generated coordinate algebras with $\kappa(s)$.

source.place: Tags 01W3, 01W4, 01W5; properness and finite-type permanence for the graph projection.

proof.text: Regard $r$ as a $Y$-morphism, since $pr=b$. Its source is proper over $Y$ via $b$, and its target is separated over $Y$ via $p$ by step 4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] gives that $r$ is proper. Its image is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and contains $U$ by step 3. Schematic density of $U$ in $\Gamma$ implies topological density: a nonempty open disjoint from $U$ would have its structure sheaf inject into zero. Hence the closed image of $r$ is all of $\Gamma$, so $r$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed; closed image of the common model and generic schematic density.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and put $k=\kappa(s)$. The maps $r_s:W_s\to\Gamma_s$ and $p_s:\Gamma_s\to Y_s$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b); $r_s$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. These are finite-type $k$-schemes, and every component of $W_s$ has dimension one by the item. If a fibre $(\Gamma_s)_y$ had positive dimension, [lem-trf-proper-curve-image-positive-fibre-component] would give a closed $y\in Y_s$ and a component $Z\subset W_s$ with $b_s(Z)=\{y\}$ and $\dim r_s(Z)=1$. The item hypothesis gives $a_s(Z)=\{x\}$ for a point $x\in X_s$. This point is closed: $Z$ is closed and $a_s$ is proper, again by proper base change and [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0B2L, component/dimension count on the fibre of the graph closure; application of the new statement with T=W_s, G=Gamma_s and Y=Y_s.

proof.text: The closed points $x,y$ have residue fields finite over $k$: in affine charts their residue fields are quotients of finite-type $k$-algebras by maximal ideals, hence [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] applies. By [lem-trf-closed-point-residue-immersion] they define closed subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\subset X_s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\subset Y_s$. Their fibre product over $C_s$ is a closed subscheme $F\subset P_s$ by closed-immersion base change and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b),(e). Put $z=f_s(x)=g_s(y)$. Explicitly $F=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(z)}\kappa(y))$; its ring is a quotient of $\kappa(x)\otimes_k\kappa(y)$ and so finite-dimensional over $k$. Each prime quotient of a finite-dimensional algebra is a finite-dimensional domain; multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective, so that quotient is a field. Thus every prime is maximal and $F$ has dimension zero. The image $i_s r_s(Z)$ lies in $|F|$, since its two projections are $x,y$. Closed immersions preserve subspace topologies, so $\dim r_s(Z)\leq0$, contradicting step 6. Therefore every fibre of every $p_s$ has dimension at most zero.

source.place: Agent calculation for a graph image whose two projections are closed points; finite residue extensions by the cited Zariski lemma, then finite-dimensional tensor algebra.

proof.text: For $y\in Y$ over $s\in S$, the fibre $\Gamma_y$ is canonically $(\Gamma_s)_y$, by associativity of fibre products and the residue-field map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Step 7 shows its dimension is at most zero. At each point of a nonempty such fibre the local topological dimension is exactly zero: it is nonnegative, and every subspace of a space with no strict specialization chain has dimension at most zero. Since $p$ is of finite type by step 4, [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] makes it locally quasi-finite. It is proper by step 4, so [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes it finite. Also $p_\eta$ is an isomorphism by step 2; the generic opens in both $Y$ and $\Gamma$ are schematically dense by steps 1--2. Thus $p$ is a finite $\eta$-modification, with no Noetherian-base hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0397, lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0; More on Morphisms Tag 02LS, proper locally quasi-finite implies finite.

proof.text: By the stated $\eta$-normality of $Y$, the finite $\eta$-modification $p$ is an isomorphism. Define $h=q_\Gamma p^{-1}:Y\to X$. From $pr=b$ and $q_\Gamma r=a$ we get $hb=a$. The two projections of $P$ satisfy $fq=gp_0$, hence $fh=g$. Thus $h$ is a $C$-morphism, and on the generic fibre $h_\eta=f_\eta^{-1}g_\eta$.

proof.text: If $h_1,h_2:Y\to X$ are $C$-morphisms with $h_ib=a$, then the generic-fibre isomorphism $b_\eta$ gives $(h_1)_\eta=(h_2)_\eta$. Since $f$ is proper, its diagonal is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; their equalizer is its pullback, hence a closed subscheme of $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Its defining ideal restricts to zero on $Y_\eta$. On each affine open of $Y$, step 1 proved that the coordinate ring injects into its generic localization, so this ideal is zero. The equalizer is all of $Y$, proving $h_1=h_2$.
